editorial_reason: ProofWiki Definition:Noetherian Module gives three equivalent definitions over a commutative ring with identity. The finite-generation, ascending-chain and maximal conditions quantify over submodules, not arbitrary subsets and not ideals of an unrelated ring. When R is an R-module, submodules correspond to ideals, supporting the independently screened Noetherian-ring-as-module formulation after the separately sourced module definition exists. The condition for submodules is not itself a circular definition of a Noetherian module.

The ProofWiki source requires a module structure on the subset inherited from M, along with closure under the scalar operation. In standard algebra these requirements are equivalent to being an additive subgroup stable under all scalar multiplication. The definition does not say that any arbitrary subset of M is automatically a submodule and must not be merged with an ideal of a ring, even though ideals are special submodules of R.

ProofWiki's direct definition explicitly assumes S is nonempty and defines the discrete topology as its entire power set. The same construction also makes sense for the empty set, but that extension has not been separately cited in this batch. The nonempty version is sufficient to define the two-point discrete target in the connectedness characterization. Do not confuse a discrete topological space with a discrete category.

ProofWiki explicitly separates continuity everywhere by preimages of open sets and continuity at each point by open-neighborhood containment. The two formulations are equivalent for arbitrary topological spaces, including the empty-domain case. The pointwise statement quantifies over every x∈X; continuity does not require a bijection, openness of f itself, or metric epsilon-delta arguments. The previously inaccessible guessed URL was incorrect; this checked page is the precise accessible source.
